summary.outcome: Planning completed successfully: 5 plans across 3 waves covering all 6 requirements (including a scope expansion adding batch+drag move parity), passing plan-check after one revision round. Execution reached Wave 3 (3/5 plans done) with the transcript ending mid-dispatch of 49-04; PR-QA, push, and PR creation had not yet occurred.

repo: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — takes raw key bytes with no owner/recipient distinction, reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case.

`share_keys` entries are keyed by `itemId` (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move; download path resolves by `k.itemId === item.id` regardless of parent.
`adoptSharedFolderResult` must be called only once (for the source folder result, using `live.ipnsName`); calling it for the destination would corrupt the rendered shared-folder view.
`sdkCore.moveItem` throws `'An item with this name already exists in destination'` on collision (sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:346) — no auto-rename needed, just propagate the error.
`SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) only listed 7 Phase 48 methods; both `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` had to be added.

File IPNS key for shared-folder re-encryption must come from `share_keys keyType:'file-ipns'`, NOT `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` (owner-wrapped; recipient cannot decrypt it) — mirrors the `updateSharedFileHandler` pattern.

Batch move in the private vault is a web-layer loop pattern: `useFileBrowserActions` selection Set → `handleBatchMoveConfirm` → `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems` → loops single-item `client.moveItem`. No dedicated SDK batch method exists.

After adding new public methods to the SDK package, the SDK dist must be rebuilt before the web package's `tsc -b` gate; the web compiler checks the built `dist/`, not source. New methods land in `client.d.ts`, not `index.d.ts` (which is a barrel re-export).
`useSharedWriteOps.test.ts` already exists and can be extended rather than creating a new test file for new shared write handler coverage.
The intel API surface regex extractor is unpopulated — the artifact is HINT-only and can be safely omitted from planner prompts when RESEARCH.md already carries verified symbol refs.

code.finding: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` is key-agnostic (raw key bytes, no owner/recipient distinction) — safe to call for shared-folder moves without modification.
Collision policy is throw: `'An item with this name already exists in destination'` — propagates through `runWrite` → `p.setError`; no auto-rename logic needed.
`SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist — must be kept up to date when new methods are added to `SharedFolderClient`; easy to miss since TypeScript won't error until the method is actually referenced.

workflow: GSD plan-phase chain: research → Nyquist VALIDATION.md → pattern-mapper → planner (opus) → plan-checker → revision loop until clean. Each step is a discrete subagent; the orchestrator coordinates.
Sequential within-wave execution (no worktrees) is more reliable than parallel-worktree mode for autonomous/AFK runs — the parallel merge-back protocol has known cwd-drift and merge-base footguns.

Scope expansion (batch+drag) can be folded into a phase cleanly by editing ROADMAP + CONTEXT before the planner is spawned — no re-research needed if private-vault analogs exist and are verified first.
Plan-checker is worth running even after a seemingly clean planner pass: caught a real gap (REQ-3 had no dedicated web unit test, so its VALIDATION wave would pass vacuously).
Planner-revision subagents cannot commit because `gsd-tools` is not on their PATH — always commit revision artifacts manually after the subagent returns.
The web package has no `typecheck` npm script; use `tsc -b` directly from the web package directory.

Disabling `commit.gpgsign` locally (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) prevents 1Password signer wedging during autonomous runs, but requires a signed rebase before merge if the repo enforces signed commits on PRs.
CodeRabbit flow is two-phase: CLI review (`coderabbit review --agent`) before pushing; automatic GitHub review comment after PR creation → `/resolve-pr-reviews` to address inline comments.
